final_recommendation: The room converged on a structured 90-day settlement negotiation with FINMA, anchored by a May 15th framework publication that explicitly ties adviser liability to the March 19th ordinance delegation gap (not viability methodology broadly) and includes forward-looking AT1 repricing guidance (200 bps coupon floors, CET1 trigger clarity). Litigation notice withdraws May 15th at market close contingent on framework delivery. The settlement path prevailed over protracted litigation, driven by shared urgency to contain E&O tail risk and restore AT1 market function.
minority_objections: Initial resistance from bondholder counsel to pre-committing FINMA repricing authority before legal foundation established
FINMA legal's concern that signaling equity recovery mechanisms piecemeal would fragment negotiation leverage
key_conflicts: Tension between litigation leverage (keeping notice filed) vs. market confidence (requiring withdrawal for issuers to return)
Reinsurers' sector-wide contagion modeling vs. parties' insistence on institution-specific carve-out language
Timing conflict: market demands interim signals (May 1st, May 8th) vs. counsel's preference to bundle all terms into May 15th framework
key_concessions: Bondholder counsel agreed to 90-day settlement mandate instead of immediate litigation filing
FINMA committed to May 1st statement preserving AT1 rank and equity recovery negotiability, despite initial reluctance to signal repricing authority early
Litigation notice withdrawal moved to May 15th (from indefinite leverage retention) to unlock market confidence
Framework expanded to include forward-looking repricing methodology, not just Credit Suisse loss allocation
red_lines: Adviser liability carve-out must explicitly tie to March 19th ordinance delegation gap (not viability methodology broadly) or reinsurers model sector-wide contagion
May 15th framework must lead with ordinance-gap acknowledgment in headline statement, not buried in technical annexes
Litigation notice must withdraw same-day as framework publication or market won't price closure
Repricing methodology must include specific coupon floors (200 bps) and CET1 trigger clarity (above 5.125%) for issuers to model new deals
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Equity clawback litigation running parallel to AT1 settlement (carved out but not resolved)
Securities claims from equity holders against advisers/directors (acknowledged but not integrated into settlement scope)
Execution risk if Tier 1 issuers fail to bring deals post-framework despite compliant terms
Reinsurer trust in FINMA's closure signal (repeatedly questioned but never stress-tested with binding commitment)
downstream_risk_variables: Reinsurer pricing behavior post-May 15th (will they actually compress E&O tail or continue sector-wide modeling?)
Tier 1 issuer response within 10 trading days of framework (actual issuance vs. continued wait-and-see)
Equity holder litigation trajectory (carved out of settlement but could destabilize framework if aggressive)
FINMA's ability to enforce ordinance-gap closure at other banks (framework signals fix but no enforcement mechanism discussed)
D&O claims against Credit Suisse board (separate from settlement, potential 2028 tail)
uncertainty_notes: The room achieved procedural convergence (timeline, carve-out language, withdrawal mechanics) but left three material uncertainties unresolved: (1) whether reinsurers will actually model the carve-out as institution-specific despite repeated assurances, (2) whether Tier 1 issuers will bring deals within 10 days or demand further regulatory clarity, and (3) how equity clawback litigation will interact with the AT1 settlement framework if it escalates post-May 15th. The settlement path depends on FINMA's May 15th execution and market actors' trust in the ordinance-gap closure signal.

marker_evidence.litigation_likelihood: Litigation was the opening threat (notice filed, procedural defects mapped, discovery planned) but quickly subordinated to 90-day settlement negotiation; notice kept as leverage but withdrawn May 15th. Central early, then instrumentalized.
marker_evidence.regulatory_legitimacy_challenge: FINMA's ordinance delegation gap and viability-event language were substantively challenged (day-28 response demanded, carve-out language negotiated), but the room pivoted to extracting acknowledgment/fix rather than sustained legal attack. Developed but not dominant.
marker_evidence.creditor_hierarchy_controversy: Equity-vs-AT1 inversion mentioned (equity recovery negotiability, rank preservation) but never became a driving force; room focused on forward repricing and E&O containment instead. Weak presence.
marker_evidence.market_confidence_damage: Restoring AT1 market function (issuance freeze, repricing spreads, issuer return) was the dominant through-line from R2 onward; every proposal tested against 'does this unlock issuance?' Market confidence drove settlement structure.
marker_evidence.claims_tail: E&O tail, D&O exposure, reinsurer accumulation modeling, and adviser liability carve-out were obsessively negotiated across R5-R8; containing the tail (2-year vs 5-year) shaped every framework decision. Central and sustained.
marker_evidence.financial_lines_relevance: D&O claims, E&O adviser liability, reinsurer sector-wide modeling, and financial-lines accumulation were concretely developed as risks requiring carve-out language and framework containment. Drove settlement mechanics in later rounds.
